title: Diwali in Dubai 2026: Where to Book, From Dhs99 Feasts to Dhs1,260 Tastings
excerpt: Indian restaurants across Dubai have published Diwali menus for Sunday, November 8 — here are the verified prices, dates and dishes, from Ziya's Dhs99 Swad Mahal to Avatara's 17-course dinner.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026 in Dubai, and Indian restaurants across the city are running festive menus from Dhs99 to Dhs1,260 per person.
  • The best-value verified option is Ziya at Anantara Downtown, with its Swad Mahal vegetarian menu at Dhs99 per person from November 1 to 8.
  • Premium picks include Gymkhana Dubai's first Diwali tasting menu at Dhs495 on November 8, Jamavar's Chahar Bagh feast at Dhs395 vegetarian and Dhs425 non-vegetarian until November 11, and Avatara's 12-course lunch or 17-course dinner from Dhs960.
  • Most one-day menus are only on November 8, so booking ahead matters — several venues list a single lunch and dinner service for Diwali day.

Dubai's Indian restaurants have set their menus for Diwali, which falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026. Three independent guides — What's On, FACT Magazines and BBC Good Food Middle East — list overlapping festive menus, and the prices below are the ones at least two of them agree on, or that a single guide states in full.

The premium end

Avatara, the one-Michelin-starred vegetarian restaurant in Dubai Hills Estate, is serving a 12-course lunch and a 17-course dinner on November 8, with dishes including wasabi greens with daikon and ghevar, and butternut with black lime. Prices start at Dhs960 per person for the non-alcoholic package and Dhs1,260 with alcohol, according to What's On and FACT.

Gymkhana Dubai in DIFC is marking its first Diwali in the city with a one-day tasting menu on November 8 at Dhs495 per person. FACT lists the dishes as aloo chaat, Amritsari shrimp and queenies, chicken butter masala and beef cheek vindaloo, served with saffron pilau, dal maharani and khameeri roti.

Jamavar, in the Dubai Opera District, has paired with Indian design house Good Earth for 'Diwali: A Feast in Chahar Bagh', a tasting menu running until November 11 at Dhs395 for the vegetarian menu and Dhs425 for the non-vegetarian menu. All three guides list dishes including Nazakat ke Bhalle, Bhatti ka Paneer and Wild Mushroom Galouti.

Ishq by Chef Nimish Bhatia, the 22-seat restaurant next to Raffles Dubai at Wafi, is offering a 13-course tasting menu on November 8 at Dhs799 per person, with an optional beverage pairing for Dhs500. The vegetarian menu includes crackling paneer kebab and Gulabo khichdi with seared morels and truffle; the non-vegetarian menu includes Kashmiri lamb.

Mid-range and family options

Kinara by Vikas Khanna at JA Lake View Hotel serves a set menu by Chef Ashish Kumar on November 7 and 8 from 6pm to 10.30pm at Dhs350 per person, with a welcome drink, live entertainment and a complimentary sweet box. Children aged 5 to 12 get the set menu at half price and children under 5 dine free, according to What's On and BBC Good Food Middle East.

Varq at Taj Exotica Resort & Spa on the Palm runs the longest window: a festive set menu from Dhs275 per person, from October 30 to November 15, with entertainment and complimentary welcome drinks. The same hotel's Palm Kitchen hosts a Diwali buffet on November 8 from 6.30pm to 10.30pm at Dhs235 for adults and Dhs120 for children aged 6 to 11, What's On reported.

Mausam at Dubai Mall serves its Flavours of India all-day set menu on November 8 at Dhs189 per person, overlooking the Burj Khalifa and Dubai Fountain. Bombay Borough in DIFC runs a tasting menu from November 6 to 11 at Dhs295 per person, according to BBC Good Food Middle East.

The budget pick

Ziya at Anantara Downtown Dubai Hotel is the clear value option. Its Swad Mahal vegetarian menu — solkadhi welcome drink, papdi chaat, khaman dhokla, shahi paneer with saag, panchmel dal, rice, breads, kaju katli and puran poli — costs Dhs99 per person and runs from November 1 to 8, all three guides confirm.

Beyond the table

For readers who want a celebration rather than a set menu, FACT lists the Noor: Festival of Lights at Al Seef on November 7 and 8 from 6pm to 11pm, and a Diwali Mela with an India Pavilion, a kids' corner and street food at Global Village from November 6 to 10. Both sit alongside the restaurant options for families planning the whole weekend.

Prices are per person as published by the guides and venues may change them; check the venue before booking, particularly for the one-day November 8 menus, which are the most likely to sell out.
